H013: investigate ONE revised exact global-resultant selector (no individual-root slab). Let f be the stated monic base-m degree-d polynomial for N, coefficient height A, H the sieving-element height, and C0=(3H)^d(d+1)A². Enumerate all primitive irreducible integer quadratics g=aX²+bX+c with positive a and height<=H. Keep g only if |Res(f,g)|^(5d)*N^6 <= C0^(5d), i.e. eta=2/5. Charge every coefficient tuple, failed filter and exact arithmetic step. The original model now needs 3a0>=b0+tau+[14/(5delta)+a0 delta]/(3b0), max(3a0,2b0)<c_C; a0,b0 are L constants, not coefficients. A lower survivor count alone is not smoothness, rank or useful-factor probability. No full siever.

Find an analytic density/height obstruction or a constructive family that could meet the charged inequality. In particular audit whether all apparent norm gain merely comes from g of smaller actual Mahler measure/height, hence sacrifices the coefficient population already priced by the baseline; do not assume this universally. Correlated cancellation between f and g may change it but must be constructed/counted, not called free lattice reduction. If finite counting is useful, choose a representative small parameter grid, freeze it and all rejection rules BEFORE the only <=60-second run, retain exact inputs, all counts, partial/unstarted cases and source hashes. Parameter changes require a new round. Give both declared cube height and actual coefficient/Mahler bounds; huge slack in C0 at tiny d can make finite admission meaningless.

A possible exact fast arithmetic route to check, not an established lemma supplied as oracle: reduce a^(d-1)f modulo g to UX+V using scaled integer powers, then Res(f,g)=(c U²-b U V+a V²)/a^(d-1), with exact division. This appears to give O(d) scalar recurrence work per quadratic at polynomial widths; verify against independent Sylvester determinants on a tiny frozen set before relying on it. It avoids floating roots but does not reduce the H³ scan. A correct slower exact resultant is also acceptable. No factor library, floating equality, hidden factor data, or uncharged full norm factorization. Only after a credible counting result should smoothness processing be considered; default trial division costs an extra B factor and cannot be dropped.

Deliver the most decisive result available: an executable selector and honest limited count, a self-contained rejection for its parameter regime, or a concrete constructive mechanism with full selection cost. Do not spend the whole task restating an unimplemented fast oracle. Technical sources must be checked primary sources. Any positive complexity claim needs a new independent review. Verified improvement remains NONE unless complete evidence supports changing it.
